reviews.review_title: Did not expect this game to be $10
reviews.review_description:
After the trailer I figured this was going to be an expensive game.  Then I saw it was $10 and bought it on the spot. Somehow it’s even bigger in the headset: tanks, bugs and flying enemies...Gun games are always fun in VR because there's almost a extra skill factor here.  (Especially being able to use two guns at once.).   Their discord convinced me to buy it because of how active the devs are and it seems like they have a lot of updates planned already.   If ur looking for a good value purchase on your headset, this is my rec.

The intro on the ship for the first play is a little long and wish I could speed through it..but excited to have a new game to play

reviews.review_title: Intense VR shooter that's good fun
reviews.review_description:
I'm having a blast with this game.  The action is fast-paced, and it definitely earns its "Intense" comfort rating.  There are a few difficulty modes to choose from, and while the easier difficulties are definitely less intense, I feel like the hardest difficulty is where the game really shines.  There are swarms of aberrants (alien bugs) everywhere you go, and this, combined with having your fellow soldiers to look after, makes the combat hectic and victory feel satisfying.

The environments look great, and the missions have some randomization to them, so they don't always feel the same.  As you advance through the game, new aberrant types are introduced, but they aren't just limited to the later missions.  They're also retrofitted into the earlier ones, giving you a reason to revisit the missions you've already completed, and making some of the earlier ones a real challenge when you revisit them later.

The combat is really satisfying, with a rapid-fire pistol, rifle, marksman rifle, and gloves that allow you to launch projectiles by throwing punches. The weapons are all upgradeable, each have their own strengths and weaknesses, and you're able to dual-wield two of them at once (including the gloves), which is handy when you're getting swarmed from both the ground and the air.  The NPC soldiers are surprisingly capable, putting up a decent fight, rather than just being helpless targets that you need to babysit the whole time.  I'm still working through the first campaign, but I'm pretty much still at the beginning, and there's a lot more to go.

I've played like 10yrs of VR and always enjoyed wave shooters and that pure classic arcade blasting fantasy. Age of Arca does it really well, my sweaty headset can attest to that! Its a super satisfying game to just boot up the headset and get blasting in, and while i haven't finished the campigns yet im excited to see what else they add next

I’ve played FPS games for years, but this was my first time playing a shooter in VR, and honestly my first VR game ever. This was such a fun place to start. 

It’s fun pulling the guns off my own body. It’s so satisfying, reaching to my side or over my shoulder and actually grabbing the weapon makes it feel real in a way a button press never does. I like how immersive it feels. 

There was a learning curve for sure since I haven’t played a lot of VR games since 2019 and there were a couple times where I felt a lil queasy (which is why I didn’t continue playing VR after playing a bit in 2019) BUT this game for the most part felt okay on my body. I felt apprehensive because of my experience with VR before but this felt easier to deal with and also a great workout.

Age of Arca is one of the most fun shooters I've played recently. The battles feel massive. 

Swarms of Aberrants pour in from every direction and you really feel like an elite space marine holding the line. Cinematic and plays fast, and I keep coming back for one more round. Highly recommended if you want big, fast paced, explosive combat!!

Love the ghosts of mars and starship troopers vibes!! 1010
Haven’t had this much fun since the first time playing Robo Recall
